top.line: RiskMandate and the ABP, for the person who decides
top.para: A reader found the pages hard, saw the value in reporting what an agent can do, guessed it did not cover commercial agents or real time, and asked how it gets into the room. This answers all four: what it is, why it stays out of the agent's path, which agents it covers, and five ways in.

in-short.line: It records what an agent can reach; others enforce
in-short.para: For one agent in one deployment: the grant, the mandate, the gap and what stands in the way. It never sits in the agent's path, already covers commercial agents, measures the enterprise-assistant oversharing gap, extends to decision and workflow policies, and enters through questions already asked.

pages.line: The pages are precise, not clear; this is the short version
pages.para: The sites were written in the vocabulary the work needed: grant, mandate, delta, barrier, a 23-word grammar. That criticism is fair, and this article is the ten-minute version for someone deciding whether it matters.

what.line: Grant, mandate, delta and barrier, for one agent
what.para: An agent's credential lets it do far more than the job. The behaviour policy records what it can reach, what was authorised, the authority nobody accepted, and the barrier on each capability. Only a boundary enforced by something the grant does not include bounds anything; a prompt line does not.

inspect.line: It reports what an agent can actually do
inspect.para: Thirteen prompts in the assistant you already use list its tools, draft what you wanted in three lists, and write the gap down; the list is longer than the tile that sold it. That is a self-report; paid levels measure the credential, and the reviewed level is signed by a person.

commercial.line: Commercial agents covered, with whose barrier each is
commercial.para: The library covers Claude with Gmail and Microsoft 365, ChatGPT, Claude Desktop, Google Workspace, Dropbox, n8n, Claude Code and GitHub Actions, from vendor pages or measurement. No Rovo, Copilot or Glean vault exists yet. Each barrier is marked as yours or a vendor product decision.

oversharing.line: Rovo grants no new access; four risks sit around it
oversharing.para: Atlassian says Rovo honours existing permissions. The risks: over-shared content becomes easy to find; agents run from automations act with the rule creator's access, which Atlassian calls intended; anyone can build agents by default; and a reported injection can send data out. As a behaviour policy, that is the delta, with five due-diligence questions.

realtime.line: Not in the path, on purpose; runtimes enforce
realtime.para: RiskMandate reads and models, with no enforcement point to slow or break an agent, which is why it can describe agents it cannot control. Enforcement belongs to gateways, hooks and runtimes: an ABP was compiled into Ruflo's rules and enforced live on memory operations.

decisions.line: Beyond reach: who decides, on what evidence
decisions.para: A behaviour policy answers may it, not is it right. Decision and workflow policies add who decides and in what order. The Northstar refund twin shows it in five minutes: a limit and good logs overpay $458 in a day; three policies get all thirteen cases right.

room.line: Five questions already on somebody's desk
room.para: Few people see how fast agents move, so nobody asks for an agent risk tool. The way in is a question with a deadline: a vendor contract, a customer's security questionnaire, an insurance renewal, the board's risk appetite, or twenty minutes with your own assistant. None needs anyone to understand agents first.

back.line: Tell us which question you are asked
back.para: Readers in those rooms are asked which question they face and what answer would help. For an enterprise assistant like Rovo, the early access programme builds its behaviour policy for one real agent, in exchange for corrections.

limits.line: No Rovo vault, no enforcement, and weak self-reports
limits.para: No Rovo, Copilot or Glean vault exists; the Rovo shape is from Atlassian's pages. RiskMandate does not enforce. The insurance argument and the injection report are others' claims, and self-reports are marked as weak evidence.

sources.line: riskmandate.ai, abp.sgit.ai, and Atlassian's own pages
sources.para: Both sites as read on 18 October 2026, Atlassian's Rovo privacy, trust, connector, governance and tracker pages, Microsoft's oversharing guidance, and a third-party injection report.
